title: PADIS Bundle & RASS
sources: Critical Vector — ICU Pocket Guide: PADIS Bundle (SCCM/PADIS 2025)
SCCM PADIS guideline (2018) + 2025 update; ICU Liberation / ABCDEF bundle

changelog.change: Initial entry — the PADIS domains + tools + targets, the RASS scale, and the ICU sedative/analgesic quick-reference. 2025 update: dexmedetomidine over propofol for light sedation in ventilated adults; Anxiety added as a 6th domain.

summary: Analgesia FIRST — treat pain before titrating sedation. Target RASS −1 to 0 for most ventilated patients. Assess each domain with a validated tool every shift. Avoid benzodiazepines (delirium). PADIS 2025: dexmedetomidine is suggested over propofol for light sedation in ventilated adults, and anxiety is a new sixth domain (non-pharmacologic strategies first).

rows: RASS −1 to 0 (deeper only for a specific indication)
Progressive daily mobility (out of bed as early as safe)
Minimise nocturnal interruptions; cluster care; day/night light cues
Non-pharmacologic first — music, VR, family presence, reassurance

body.text: Wrap it in the ABCDEF bundle: Assess/treat pain · Both spontaneous awakening + breathing trials · Choice of light sedation (dexmedetomidine or propofol, not a benzo) · Delirium assess/prevent/manage · Early mobility · Family engagement. Bundle adherence is associated with lower 7-day mortality and less delirium.

rows: Pulls at or removes tubes / catheters; aggressive
Frequent non-purposeful movement; fights the ventilator
Not fully alert; sustained (> 10 s) awakening to voice
Movement or eye-opening to voice, no eye contact
No response to voice; movement to physical stimulation
No response to voice or physical stimulation

α2-agonist — cooperative sedation, no respiratory depression; bradycardia / hypotension. PADIS 2025: preferred over propofol for light sedation in MV adults. Can't reliably sedate a genuinely agitated patient alone (SPICE III)
GABA — fast on/off, easy neuro checks. PRIS if > 4–5 mg/kg/hr for > 48 h — trend triglycerides q72h, watch for unexplained metabolic acidosis / new arrhythmia
Benzodiazepine — AVOID for routine sedation (delirium, prolonged wake-up). Reserve for status epilepticus or severe alcohol withdrawal
Opioid-sparing, bronchodilator; increases secretions; historically ICP concern is not supported in sedated/ventilated patients
The default ICU opioid; hepatic metabolism, accumulates with prolonged infusion (context-sensitive half-time)
~5× the potency of morphine; safer than morphine in renal failure (no active metabolite accumulation)
